claim_text: Water's density is roughly 1 gram per milliliter, and it changes with temperature and dissolved substances.

evidence.text: The density of water is roughly 1 gram per milliliter but, this changes with temperature or if there are substances dissolved in it.
Ice is less dense than liquid water which is why your ice cubes float in your glass.

claim_text: Heavy-water ice sinks in normal water.

evidence.text: Ice is less dense than liquid water which is why your ice cubes float in your glass.
Heavy water is indeed heavier than normal water (which contains a tiny amount of heavy water molecules naturally), and heavy-water ice will sink in normal water.

claim_text: Evaporation changes liquid water into water vapor.

evidence.text: Evaporation is the process that changes liquid water to gaseous water (water vapor).
Condensation is the process of water vapor turning back into liquid water.

claim_text: Water cannot evaporate at its freezing point; evaporation only happens at its boiling point.

evidence.text: Evaporation is the process that changes liquid water to gaseous water (water vapor).
Water easily evaporates at its boiling point (212° F, 100° C) but evaporates much more slowly at its freezing point because of the heat energy required to evaporate the water.

claim_text: Raising one kilogram of water by one degree Celsius requires 4,184 joules of heat.

evidence.text: Water has to absorb 4,184 Joules of heat (1 kilocalorie) for the temperature of one kilogram of water to increase 1°C.
For the sake of comparison, it only takes 385 Joules of heat to raise 1 kilogram of copper 1°C.
